name: Can I move the toilet in a small bathroom?

mainEntity.name: Can I move the toilet in a small bathroom without making the room feel tighter or breaking code clearance requirements?
mainEntity.text: Can I move the toilet in a small bathroom without making the room feel tighter or breaking code clearance requirements?

acceptedAnswer.text: Moving a toilet in a small bathroom is possible, but the new layout has to respect clearance requirements and leave enough room to use the fixture comfortably. The biggest constraints are the drain line location, wall framing, and the spacing needed around the toilet and nearby vanity or shower. In compact Los Angeles homes, a toilet move can quickly create a chain reaction: the door swing may need to change, the vanity may need to shrink, or the shower may need to be reshaped. Before committing, measure the room carefully and test the layout on paper or in a 3D plan. A design that looks good on a sketch can still fail in real life if the toilet, door, and shower all compete for the same circulation space.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but the new location must still allow proper clearances around the toilet, including side-to-side width and front clearance. In a small bathroom, moving the toilet is often limited by wall structure, drain routing, and whether there is enough space to keep the room comfortable and functional.
